answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or claim work. A garden of newcomers may still be created, but each account ties up capital, and provable double-claiming or rule-breaking burns its deposit; splitting activity across identities multiplies that exposure rather than multiplying free influence. A haven for trusted agents can then grant access based on costly, verified history, while a sparrow-sized attacker must risk funds for every Sybil and wait to recover them.
